title: Perceptual Context Compression — proposal (scratch)
content:
Goal:
Build a lightweight, lossy compression layer for per-user context blobs that prioritizes perceptual/salient content over verbatim token fidelity. The idea is to reduce token count sent to hosted inference (and reduce billable tokens) while preserving downstream model behavior for common user-flows (summarization, follow-up questions, simple retrieval).

Why this?
- Some context is redundant or low-salience for model decisions (boilerplate, repetitive dialogs, system meta).
- Pure token-based truncation wastes high-salience bits.
- Storing and transmitting dense compressed summaries could cut cost and latency for mobile/offline-first clients.

High-level approach:
1) Create a salience scoring pass over recent context (approximate attention-worthiness using cheap heuristics + small local model).
2) Partition tokens into: high-salience (keep), medium (compress via phrase-level substitution / placeholders), low (drop or represent by aggregate metadata).
3) Optionally attach compact provenance hints to help the model reconstruct tone or factual anchors.
4) Provide a decompression shim on the inference side that expands placeholders into stochastic reconstructions or prompts the model to "assume X".

Design notes / components:
- Local preprocessor API (client-side)
  - compress_context(context_text, policy) -> compressed_blob, meta
  - policy = {"target_tokens": 512, "salience_model": "tiny-attention-v0", "preserve_entities": true, "max_placeholder_ratio": 0.25}

- Compressed blob schema (compact):
  - proto: version id, compressed_payload (base64), entity_index (list of top N entities), salience_map (sparse), provenance_digest
  - payload is a mix of raw tokens and placeholder markers like [[P:3]] meaning "placeholder 3"

- Server decompression layer (Redwood-side)
  - validate signature -> optional partial decode -> expand placeholders using local reconstruction model or inline prompt template; fallback to sending original full context if expansion confidence low.

ASCII flow diagram:

  [Client app] --(full text)--> [Compressor] --(compressed_blob)-> [Redwood API / decompress shim] --> [Model runtime]
  
  compressor steps: tokenize -> salience score -> chunk -> compress/replace -> fingerprint -> sign

API shape sketches (proto/REST examples):
- POST /v1/context/compress
  body: {"user_id":"1234","context":"...","policy":{...}}
  response: {"blob_id":"b_abc","blob":"<base64>","estimated_tokens": 420}

- POST /v1/infer with compressed blob:
  body: {"model":"gptx-1","context_blob":"b_abc","decompression_policy":"eager|lazy", "fallback":"send-full-on-fail"}

Config knobs (sketch):
- target_tokens: target length after compression (soft)
- preserve_entities: bool (always keep named entities in plain text)
- placeholder_density: fraction of placeholders allowed
- deterministic_reconstruction: bool (affects reproducibility)
- salience_thresholds: mapping of score->action

Reconstruction strategies (server):
- deterministic fill: rehydrate placeholders with exact saved snippets (if stored)
- generative fill: prompt local LM to paraphrase by instruction: "Replace [[P:3]] with a concise paraphrase preserving entity and sentiment."
- instruction-only: keep placeholders and include meta in system prompt: "Context has placeholders: P:3 -> user described recent purchase of X."

Evaluation plan / metrics:
- Intent preservation: %same-top-1-intent on downstream classifier compared to full context (target >= 95%)
- Response similarity: BLEU/ROUGE on deterministic tasks, behavioral tests for safety/regression
- Cost delta: tokens saved / latency change
- Failure modes: hallucination increase post-compression, entity drift

Experiment ideas / small proofs:
- 1: Heuristic salience (TF*IDF-ish + recency boost) + placeholder substitution -> measure on 10k annotated dialogs
- 2: Tiny local salience model (1–2M params) trained to predict attention weights from full model; compare to heuristic
- 3: Keep entity table + provenance digest; test retrievals for factual QA

Open questions / risks:
- Does generative reconstruction leak PII if placeholders lose exact text? (mitigation: don't generative-fill for identified PII)
- How to version blobs across client versions? Need proto+schema migration strategy.
- Privacy: need opt-in and explicit consent; keep blob encryption and KMS keys per-user.
- Legal/regulatory: stored compressed summaries may still be considered customer data.

Next steps / TODOs (short):
- prototype compressor: implement TF*recency baseline (owner: Riley)
- collect 5k synthetic dialogs for offline eval (owner: Maya)
- draft API contract for engineers + security review (owner: Luca)
- add fallback policy in Redwood API (design doc ticket: GH#2548)

Notes-to-self:
- Keep placeholders human-readable when possible (helps debugging)
- Persistent entity index lets us do targeted anti-duplication across repeated contexts
- Consider an "amnesty" header: allow server to request a full context if decompression fails with high confidence penalty

References / inspiration:
- perceptual hashing work in image compression (analogy)
- hierarchical summarization papers (2023–2024)
- internal datastore-paragraph-dedup heuristics

Rough timeline (WIP):
- 2 weeks: baseline compressor + CLI tool to inspect blobs
- 4 weeks: Redwood-side decompression shim prototype (best-effort generative fill)
- 8–12 weeks: small A/B on hosted API with opt-in customer cohort

End of scratchpad.
